subject: Production SDK transition + client-side resilience checklist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme.com>, devops@acme.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production SDK transition + client-side resilience checklist

Hi Alice / Acme team,

Thanks for confirming the go window next week. Before we cut traffic to the new endpoint, I put together a short checklist focused on client-side resilience so your users don't see regressions when we switch endpoints or model variants. Attaching a printable checklist and the minimal SDK config snippets.

High-level asks for your engineers (priority order):
1) Pin current model/version in your config and enable fallback to the previous model variant for 5m after cut.
2) Implement an exponential backoff with full-jitter for 429s and 5xx: base=150ms, cap=3s, maxRetries=6.
3) Add a local circuit breaker that opens at 25% error rate over a 1m rolling window and holds for 30s before probing.
4) Respect server Retry-After if present; otherwise use client backoff above.
5) Enable our SDK’s async batching flag (batchWindowMs=20) for the chat endpoint to preserve latency under normal load.
6) Emit these metrics: request.latency.p50/p95, request.retry.count, request.circuit.state, server.ratelimit.received

Optional: enable token-preserving prefix cache in SDK if you expect repeated prompts (we added it specifically for your recommendation engine use case).

Attachments: client-resilience-checklist.pdf (walkthrough), sdk-config-snippets.txt (copy/paste ready).

Can your team confirm engineers assigned and whether you want Redwood on the cut call? We can join the first hour to watch metrics and flip rollback if needed.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — very helpful checklist. Quick clarifying q's from our side: 

1) For the fallback: when you say 'previous model variant', do you mean the exact model SHA we are on now, or a compatible quantized variant? We’d prefer exact match, but curious about automatic compatibility fallback.
2) Do you have a recommended default for circuit-breaker "half-open" probe behavior? We have existing CB libs but want consistent behavior with Redwood recommendations.
3) Any guidance on observing request-level cost delta during the first 24h so our finance/sysops can flag anomalies?

We’ll assign Priya (engineer) and Rafael (ops) to lead. We’d like Redwood on the cut call for the first 30m.

— Alice

Hi Alice — answers inline below and a few small updates to the checklist.

1) Fallback variant: prefer pinning to the exact semantic model version (e.g., model@2026-09-15-abc123). Redwood will honor a hard pin if you pass model_version in the request. Automatic fallbacks we recommend are to the most recent compatible quantized variant; Redwood will never silently downgrade without explicit fallback rules. I’ve added the exact request header we recommend in sdk-config-snippets.txt.

2) Half-open probe: recommended probe is a single request every 10s with real traffic sampling (not synthetic), and treat a single 2xx as success to close the CB. If you use bulkhead isolation, probe at lower concurrency (1-2).

3) Cost delta monitoring: enable the per-route per-token dashboard in Redwood Console for the first 24h and set an alert at +30% deviation in tokens/req or +20% in latency p95. We’ll share a pre-built alert template (link below).

Updates added to the checklist:
- Add header X-Redwood-Client-Version with the client version and deploy id for easy tracing.
- For rate-limits: if you receive 429 with no Retry-After, backoff base should be 200ms (instead of 150ms) and escalate if >10% of requests in a 5m window are 429s.

We’ll be on the cut call Monday 10/12 at 09:00 PT for the first 30 minutes. Monica and I will watch the dashboard and help triage alerts.

—Irene

Hi all — attaching a condensed checklist (client-resilience-checklist.pdf) and the exact SDK snippet we used in our internal cut this month. Copy/paste from sdk-config-snippets.txt: 

--- sdk snippet start ---
# pseudo-yaml for client-side config
redwood:
  model_version: "model@2026-09-15-abc123"  # pin to exact semantic version
  fallback_policy:
    on_error: "fallback-to-previous"
  retries:
    enabled: true
    max_retries: 6
    base_delay_ms: 200
    max_delay_ms: 3000
    jitter: "full"
  circuit_breaker:
    window_seconds: 60
    error_threshold_percent: 25
    open_duration_seconds: 30
    half_open_probe_interval_seconds: 10
  batching:
    enabled: true
    batch_window_ms: 20
  metrics:
    emit: ["latency.p95","retry.count","circuit.state"]
--- sdk snippet end ---

A few operational notes:
- During the first 30m after cut, route 10% of traffic to the new endpoint as a warm-up if you can (split at the ingress layer). If you can’t, consider progressive ramp by 25% every 5m.
- Keep a short rollback playbook: rollback = re-pin client to the previous model_version + disable batching for 10m to clear caches.

If you want, we can run a short smoke test script (5m) against your staging with the same config and share the exact logs we look for. Priya / Rafael: can you confirm staging access and a contact for the smoke-run?

Thanks — Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
